hints.junior: A 51%-confidence guess and a 99%-confidence guess looked identical once both got auto-applied — nothing in the UI told anyone the model was unsure.
hints.mid: Every model call already returns a confidence score — most integrations just never read it before deciding whether to auto-apply.
hints.staff: 95% top-line accuracy still means wrong 5% of the time — without a confidence gate, the UI can't tell that 5% apart from the 95% it should trust.

hints.junior: Toggle modes and watch which of the four suggestions apply instantly versus which one waits for you to decide.
hints.mid: The threshold here is fixed for the demo — in production it's tuned per action, not one constant for the whole product.
hints.staff: In broken mode there's zero visual signal for which applied suggestions were actually low-confidence guesses — that data existed and was thrown away.

hints.junior: High-confidence suggestions apply automatically, same as before — low-confidence ones wait in a reviewable state instead of applying blind.
hints.mid: The threshold is a product decision, not a technical constant — tune it against how costly a wrong auto-apply actually is for that action.
hints.staff: The threshold should scale with blast radius — 70% confidence is fine for a low-stakes tag, risky as a default for auto-sending a customer email.

hints.junior: A review queue nobody looks at is barely better than no gate — make accepting or rejecting a suggestion genuinely one click.
hints.mid: If reviewers accept almost everything below threshold, it's set too conservative; if they reject a lot above it, it's set too loose — track outcomes.
hints.staff: Confidence scores aren't calibrated the same across model versions — re-validate the threshold against real outcomes whenever the model changes.

sections.junior: Hey! Today's case is about an AI suggestion tool that applied every suggestion the same way, even when the model itself was barely confident in the guess.
sections.mid: Every model call that drives an auto-applied action returns a confidence score alongside its output — most integrations just never read it.
sections.staff: This isn't a model-accuracy problem, it's a UI design problem — a model with ninety-five percent accuracy is still wrong on the other five, and without a gate the UI can't tell those apart.

sections.junior: The fix is a confidence threshold: high-confidence suggestions still apply automatically, but low-confidence ones wait for a human to actually look at them first.
sections.mid: A threshold turns one uniform behavior into two: score above it auto-applies, anything below sits in a reviewable pending state with the suggestion visible but not yet committed.
sections.staff: The threshold should scale with the action's blast radius — auto-tagging a ticket at seventy percent is low-stakes, auto-sending a customer email at the same seventy percent is a much riskier default.

sections.junior: Watch four simulated suggestions with different confidence scores, and see which ones apply themselves versus which ones wait for review.
sections.mid: The threshold here is fixed for clarity — in a real system it's tuned per action, not one global constant.
sections.staff: The broken mode gives zero visual signal about which applied suggestions were actually low-confidence guesses — that information existed and was simply discarded.

sections.junior: A model's confidence score is a real signal. Use it: auto-apply the confident output, and make the rest wait for a human to say yes.
sections.mid: Gate auto-apply behind a confidence threshold — high-confidence suggestions apply automatically, low-confidence ones wait for explicit review.
sections.staff: Set the threshold per action based on blast radius, and re-validate the cutoff whenever the underlying model changes.
